description:
Outpostion is a team passionate about space exploration, innovation, and technology.
Our project, Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, is an interactive game designed to teach children about space missions.
Players take the role of mission commanders and manage resources to keep astronauts safe on the Moon or Mars.
Our goal is to make learning about space fun, engaging, and educational through interactive challenges.
summary: Outpost Zero is a NASA Space Apps game where kids command astronauts on the Moon or Mars, balancing 6 power cells for air, shields, and food using real solar flare data.
details:
Outpost Zero is an interactive, offline-ready Progressive Web App (PWA) where young players act as Outpost Commanders keeping an astronaut crew alive for 7 days on the Moon or Mars.


Core Gameplay: Commanders monitor real NASA DONKI solar flare data (C-, M-, and X-class events) and distribute 6 daily reactor power cells across Life Support, Radiation Shielding, and the Greenhouse to keep crew air, food, and health above 0%.


Interactive & Creative Features: The simulation includes a spotlight tutorial, a 6-chapter handbook, a live reactive outpost scene, end-of-day weather cinematics, mini-games, science quizzes, downloadable mission patches, and ROBO-7—an animated, voice-enabled robot.


Tools & Data Sources: Developed with HTML5, modular CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (using Canvas, Web Speech, and Service Worker APIs), powered by NASA's DONKI, OSDR, and Artemis data and refined with Claude and Gemini.


Accessibility & Impact: Translates complex space weather and resource trade-offs into hands-on STEM education with child-friendly controls, responsive layouts, screen-reader support, and reduced-motion accessibility.
